title: Practice Spotting Fake Bills
description: Bad actors sometimes try to confuse you by sending a bill for something you never bought. This psychological pattern is called 'Phantom Debt'. They want you to panic and call them to cancel it. Read the emails below and spot which ones are trying to confuse you with a fake bill, and which are calm and safe.

actions.label: 🚨 This is a fake bill (Phantom Debt)

challenges.body: Thank you for your renewal. $399.99 has been charged to your account for your 3-year tech support plan. If you did not make this purchase, call our cancellation department immediately at 1-800-555-0188.
challenges.justInTimeHint: Did you actually buy a tech support plan? Notice how they provide a phone number for you to call if you want to 'cancel'.

challenges.body: Order Confirmation: 65-Inch Smart TV. Total: $1,249.00. Will be shipped to: [Unknown Address]. To stop this shipment and dispute the charge, you must call our fraud team at 1-800-555-0922.
challenges.justInTimeHint: A huge purchase you didn't make is designed to cause panic. Are they trying to trick you into calling that specific number?

challenges.body: Your groceries have been delivered! Your total for today's order was $42.50. You can view your itemized receipt attached. Thank you for shopping with us!
challenges.justInTimeHint: This looks like a standard receipt for something you would expect. There is no demand to call a cancellation number.

gentleFailureMissedManipulation.title: A Perfect Learning Moment!
gentleFailureMissedManipulation.message: It is completely natural to panic when you see a huge bill for something you didn't buy! This is exactly how the 'Phantom Debt' pattern works. Bad actors send fake bills hoping you will call the 'cancellation number' in the email. Once you call, they try to steal your information. Remember: if you didn't buy it, you don't owe it. Never call the number in the email. You are doing wonderfully!

gentleFailureFlaggedSafe.title: Wonderful Caution!
gentleFailureFlaggedSafe.message: It is always a fantastic instinct to be careful with receipts! However, notice how calm this grocery receipt was? It didn't have a big 'call here to cancel' warning, and it wasn't for an unexpectedly huge amount. It's safe to keep for your records. Let's keep practicing!

success.title: Brilliantly Done!
success.message: You completely neutralized their 'Phantom Debt' trick! You recognized that the huge bills were designed to cause panic and trick you into calling their fake support number. By staying calm and spotting the pattern, you took away all their power. You are doing a magnificent job!
